events.title: The Berlin Wall opens
events.description: East Germans begin crossing the border freely. The change becomes a powerful symbol of a changing Europe.

events.title: Hubble launches into orbit
events.description: The space telescope leaves Earth aboard Discovery. Its first images later reveal a flaw in the main mirror.

events.title: The Soviet Union breaks apart
events.description: Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president. Independent states take the place of the union.

events.title: Web software becomes free to use
events.description: CERN releases its World Wide Web software into the public domain, helping others build on it.

what_happened_next.text:
The US share basket finished first among these choices. Exxon and Boeing also gained, while IBM lost nearly half its value. An investor could be right that computers would remain important and still lose money in a particular computer company's shares.

Boeing won a huge aircraft order from United in 1990. Exxon faced the 1989 Valdez spill, then later reported higher profits as oil prices rose during the Gulf crisis. IBM reported a record loss for 1992 as its business struggled. The three companies’ different news helps explain the risks they faced, but no one event determines a share return.

A basket of many companies spread the effect of one company's troubles. Cash and government bonds offered different paths again. None of these choices required guessing the exact order of the three featured shares.

The finished chart makes the comparison easy. In January 1989, people had company reports, news and forecasts, but no list of future winners. A confident explanation about a business could still leave out risks that appeared later.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: A new US president took office, Poland considered political change, and oil prices were rising again.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The seven paths were very different. A broad basket spread the effect of company troubles; cash and bonds earned returns through a different mix of risks.
reflection.what_faded_away: An inaugural speech and a short-term oil-price move could not reveal which investment would lead five years later.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: Nobody knew the exact path of world politics or IBM’s later decline. Being well known was not protection against losing money.

hot:1989-01:boeing.text: In October 1990, United Airlines ordered Boeing planes worth up to $22 billion, including the new 777. The order gave Boeing a large schedule of aircraft to build and deliver; its shares rose in this five-year period.

hot:1989-01:ibm.text: IBM reported a record $4.97 billion loss for 1992 after weak computer sales and large restructuring charges. Weak demand and the cost of reorganizing weighed on results; IBM shares fell during this five-year window.

hot:1989-01:exxon.text: The Exxon Valdez spilled oil into Alaska’s Prince William Sound on March 24, 1989, harming wildlife and shorelines and requiring a long cleanup. Exxon later reported record 1990 profits as oil prices jumped during the Gulf crisis; its shares rose over five years.
